lines.quote: The prayers of good people got Donald Trump elected two weeks ago.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: A story about why Trump won, not a reading of any measured object.

lines.quote: Wars with Russia and Iran are the counterattack.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Frames the coming wars as retaliation against Trump's election, treating them as a bad outcome for voters.

lines.quote: Mark Levin was at the White House today, lobbying for war with Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Concerns who is pushing for war, not the state of the war itself.

lines.quote: there is zero credible intelligence that suggests Iran is anywhere near building a bomb
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Disputes the case for war, so the war would be unjustified for Americans.

lines.quote: the real goal, which is regime change — young Americans heading back to the Middle East to topple yet another government
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Attributes hidden motives to the war's advocates, a blame story.

lines.quote: A war with Iran would amount to a profound betrayal of his supporters. It would end his presidency.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Says a war would betray the voters who chose a peace candidate.

lines.quote: The first week of a war with Iran could easily kill thousands of Americans.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Forecasts mass American deaths from Iranian missiles if war starts, with no date since the war is hypothetical.

lines.quote: It could also collapse our economy, as surging oil prices trigger unmanageable inflation.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Mechanism from war to oil prices to inflation, undated because the war is conditional.

lines.quote: An attack on Iran could very easily become a world war. We'd lose.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: very easily become a world war
lines.why: Warns that Iran's allies would escalate the war into a lost world war.

lines.quote: to box the Trump administration into a regime change war in Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Blames Levin and allies for maneuvering Trump into war.

lines.quote: Pray that Donald Trump ignores them.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: Pray that Donald Trump ignores them
lines.why: Urges Trump to reject the war camp and avoid war, a populist-right proposal.

lines.quote: The real divide is between those who casually encourage violence, and those who seek to prevent it — between warmongers and peacemakers.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: A moral frame sorting people by their stance on war, not a reading of the war.

lines.quote: anyone who's calling Donald Trump today to demand air strikes and other direct US military involvement
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Names who is pressing for US involvement and says they must answer for it, a blame line.

lines.quote: how the president's enemies are working to destroy MAGA with the war on Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Says Trump's enemies are using the war against his movement, a blame frame.

lines.quote: Senator Ted Cruz demands regime change in Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Reports a senator's position and mocks it, a line about a speaker's record rather than the war.

lines.quote: Thank God.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Relief on the day the fighting stopped, read as the war ending without escalation.

lines.quote: Thank God Trump brokered a ceasefire.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He reports the June 2025 ceasefire as a relief, so the war's end is read as good for Americans.

lines.quote: That's the last thing Mark Levin wanted.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It is about who wanted what, a point about a rival's loyalties and not about any reading.

lines.quote: Our interview with the president of Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: interview with the president of Iran
lines.why: It announces an interview and says nothing about whether the war helped or hurt Americans.

lines.quote: This is Israel's last chance to blow up Iran with America's military
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He frames the coming war as Israel using US forces for its own ends, which he treats as against American interests.

lines.quote: naturally the neocons have reached peak hysteria
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It blames a faction for pushing war and measures nothing.

lines.quote: what happens if they get their wish
lines.subject: Clayton Morris, as introduced by Tucker Carlson
lit: what happens if they get their wish
lines.why: It hints that war would be a harmful result of the neocons' wish, but gives no detail or date.

lines.quote: So mightily spread abroad your Spirit, that all peoples may be gathered under the banner of the Prince of Peace
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, quoting John Henry Newman
lines.why: Posted just after the war began, the peace prayer treats the fighting as a wrong.

lines.quote: Israel's war and what it means.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Calling it 'Israel's war' assigns ownership and blame for the war, not a reading of its effects.

lines.quote: Could this be a religious war designed to rebuild the Third Temple on the ashes of Al Aqsa?
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He casts the war as a religious project far from American interests, a bad thing for the country.

lines.quote: how this war changes American politics forever
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Saagar Enjeti
lines.why: A teaser framing the war as a lasting political turning point, without saying whether it helped or hurt.

lines.quote: Pray that the spell breaks and the world is saved.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Frames the war as a spell that endangers the world and needs breaking.

lines.quote: it should be illegal to yoke our military to a foreign power in war
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Proposes a legal ban on tying the US military to another country's wars, implying the current war did exactly that.

lines.quote: Bret Weinstein on how it happened.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Bret Weinstein
lines.why: Points to an account of how the US got pulled in, which is about causes and blame, not a reading.

lines.quote: why we actually went to war with Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Joe Kent
lines.why: Implies the stated reasons for the war are not the real ones, a question of motive rather than outcome.

lines.quote: ground troops are often followed by tyranny in the country that sends them
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Warns that sending ground troops tends to bring tyranny home, a causal claim against boots on the ground.

lines.quote: We're spending more a year on the military in adjusted dollars than we did during World War II.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: than we did during World War II
What are we getting for it?
lines.why: Cites record military spending and asks what Americans get for it, implying the war's cost is not paying off.

lines.quote: how much is going to Israel?
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: how much is going to Israel
lines.why: Asks about loyalties and where the money goes, which is blame and allegiance, not a reading.

lines.quote: the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He forecasts a nuclear escalation of the war within days, which is the war itself getting worse.

lines.quote: Netanyahu is cornered and desperate.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He blames Netanyahu and his allies in the administration for pushing the war, which is a claim about who is to blame.

lines.quote: In October alone, 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz. At this pace, a global depression is imminent.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He traces tanker damage in Hormuz to wrecked energy markets and a coming depression.

lines.quote: After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: free them to use nuclear weapons
lines.why: He describes a causal chain from an American nuclear strike to wider nuclear war.

lines.quote: the administration has quietly rewritten America's nuclear doctrine to make first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He cites a dated change in doctrine since February as making the war more dangerous.

lines.quote: Morgan Downey on the economic effects of American intervention.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: He frames the intervention as economically damaging because of how it handles energy.
